title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. Design: a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), generator = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, preregistered paired estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, analysis = exact paired McNemar-style test with paired-bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. Results (artifact-backed): planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; model_calls_used = 240; contingency: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0; baseline_success_rate = guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. All repair_applied flags are false. Two preregistration/execution issues are documented in the archive and constrain inference: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidate the preregistered independent-per-condition power assumptions, and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no rationale is recorded in the archived execution manifest. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no additional verifier-detectable benefit in this specific, artifact-grounded setting because the generator+prompt pairing already produced verifier-acceptable outputs for every task. We publish the authoritative artifacts and recommend reproducible follow-ups (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden tasks, multi-model runs, expanded verifier coverage).

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises efficiency but raises correctness and safety concerns: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, workflow order, or security predicates). Prior studies therefore recommend interposing deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects prior to execution.

Research question. Under a fully preregistered, paired confirmatory design, does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to (A) unconstrained generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding on a synthetic intent→configuration task bank?

We preregistered study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1 and executed the run under a frozen adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Contributions: (1) a complete preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation (N = 240 tasks) using gpt-5-mini and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; (2) transparent execution accounting showing shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generation per task reused across arms) and that every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier (n11 = 240), producing a degenerate null outcome; (3) confirmatory statistics (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); (4) an explicit reconciliation of preregistered power assumptions with executed semantics and a concise evidence-to-claim mapping and nearest-work comparison synthesized from the archived bibliography; and (5) operational recommendations for reproducible follow-ups to restore discordance potential and adversarial sensitivity.
sections.related_work: The experiment is situated at the intersection of three literatures. First, cross-domain surveys and empirical studies document that LLMs can hallucinate or fabricate structured artifacts and code, motivating validator-based pipelines for safety and reliability. Second, generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding techniques have been used to improve mechanically checkable properties (compilation, grammar validity) and reduce surface-level hallucinations, though reported case studies often focus on syntactic/executable gains rather than domain-specific semantic invariants. Third, NetOps-focused research emphasizes intent-driven translation, pybatfish-style verifier checks, and human-in-the-loop governance as primary controls for high-stakes changes. Representative, verified prior works informing this study include the GVR/methodology literature and recent NetOps intent-translation and verifier integration prototypes. The present run differs by (a) preregistration and a paired confirmatory design, (b) an authoritative archived analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and (c) explicit treatment of evaluation semantics (shared vs independent generation) that materially affect inferential sensitivity.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion difference of verifier-detected semantic violations). Two prespecified primary comparisons were registered: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding (Bonferroni family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) and analysis pipeline (bootstrap_seed = 1729; bootstrap_resamples = 10,000; exact McNemar two-sided test) were frozen prior to execution.

Design, tasks, and artifacts. Confirmatory sample: N = 240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks each). Task bank encodes initial device states, intent descriptions, workflow constraints, and expected final states; representative manifest entries and per-task validator traces are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json. Generator requested: gpt-5-mini (declared in execution/model_configuration.json). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing pybatfish-style checks (violation_count, violations list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation. Execution contract (frozen): generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt), maximum_model_calls budget = 480. The preregistration contains a detailed missingness and contamination plan and a fixed-N stopping rule.

Execution and controls. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter and executed the paired experiment with shared-initial-candidate semantics. Pairs with infrastructure failures would be handled by the registered 'complete_pair_primary' rules; the archived missingness summary reports zero failures. The preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation (restoring discordance potential) and targeted a detectable absolute paired reduction of 10 percentage points with N = 240; we explicitly record that this assumption is not met by the executed shared-generation semantics and therefore that preregistered power does not apply to the observed run.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed). The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 240, and model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate semantics). Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm episode accounting and provider-call audits.

Primary outcomes. The archived paired contingency table is: n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded-only accepted), n01 = 0 (baseline-only accepted), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Summary rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; 10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. All per-episode validator traces record repair_applied = false.

Statistical interpretation. The absence of any discordant pairs produces a degenerate paired test: no within-pair disagreements exist to estimate differential effect, hence p = 1.00 and the bootstrap CI collapses to a point mass at 0.0 under the preregistered analysis rules. Because the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation, that calculation is not applicable to the executed shared-generation semantics; this mismatch is deterministic and documented in the archive.

Prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison. The preregistration listed two primary comparisons; the archived execution artifacts document only the adapter-configured experiment comparing unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared-generation semantics. The prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the execution artifacts; we disclose this as a procedural deviation and limitation.

Evidence-to-claim mapping. The following concise table maps principal empirical claims to authoritative archived artifacts (artifact filenames and manifest locations are authoritative; full hash manifest is available in the execution manifest):
- Claim: All planned episodes completed and model_calls_used = 240 → execution/execution_manifest.json (planned_episode_count/completed_episode_count/model_calls_used) and analysis/missingness_summary.csv.
- Claim: Paired contingency n11 = 240; n10 = n01 = n00 = 0 → analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.
- Claim: Exact McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.0]; bootstrap_resamples = 10000; seed = 1729 → analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/results.json.
- Claim: repair_applied = false for all episodes → execution/scoring/*.json entries and execution/responses/* (validator_trace.repair_applied fields).
- Claim: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generation reused across arms), causing reduced discordance potential → preregistration document c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1 and execution/model_configuration.json; see execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Claim: prespecified C vs B comparison not executed → execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/contamination_summary.csv (no flags) (manifest records executed adapter-configured comparison only).

Nearest-work comparison (compact). For each referenced prior work we list method/target and one-line difference versus this run (references provided in the archived bibliography):
1) Generate–verify/repair method studies (e.g., generate–verify program-repair literature) — show improvements on mechanically checkable properties; difference: prior reports focus on single-repo/benchmark case studies, while our contribution is a preregistered paired confirmatory design with artifacted accounting. 
2) Grammar/schema-constrained decoding systems — increase syntactic/executable rates; difference: those studies emphasize syntactic gains, our run measures verifier-detected semantic invariants under explicit generation semantics. 
3) Recent NetOps intent-translation and verifier-integration prototypes — demonstrate architecture viability with domain-specific verifiers; difference: our study evaluates a bounded GVR intervention under a frozen paired protocol and documents how evaluation semantics (shared vs independent generation) determine measurable benefit. (A compact list of the closest verified records is supplied in the references list.)
sections.discussion:
Conservative interpretation and mechanisms. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and for this synthetic task bank and verifier, bounded GVR produced no verifier-detectable benefit because the generator+prompting pairing already produced verifier-acceptable outputs for every task. Two artifact-supported mechanisms explain the outcome: (1) task–verifier alignment: the task bank distribution, prompt, and generator together defined a space that the generator could deterministically satisfy; (2) sensitivity reduction from shared-generation semantics: reusing a single shared initial candidate across arms removes independent stochastic variation and therefore removes within-pair discordance that GVR could exploit.

Implications for evaluation practice. Demonstrating GVR efficacy requires evaluation semantics aligned with inferential assumptions. If the objective is to show that GVR reduces verifier-detected violations under generator stochasticity, the evaluation must permit independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true), include adversarial or golden-reference tasks that reliably induce verifier failures, test multiple generator families and prompt variants, and/or increase repair budgets. The archived artifacts (task manifest, RNG seeds, adapter configuration) permit deterministic reruns that implement these recommendations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation whereas the executed run used shared-generation semantics; this design mismatch undermines the preregistered power argument. Construct validity: passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not imply absence of operational risk for invariants the validator does not encode. External validity: the workload is synthetic, a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget were used; results do not generalize to other models, larger repair budgets, production topologies, or richer verifier sets. Conclusion validity: zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics. These threats and their artifact origins are documented in the archived manifests.
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment to evaluate whether a bounded Generate–Verify–Repair intervention reduces deterministic-verifier-detected semantic violations for intent→configuration synthesis. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and this synthetic workload, every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a degenerate null (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR added no verifier-detectable value in this specific, artifact-grounded setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. Two preregistration/execution deviations constrain inference: the shared-generation semantics invalidate the preregistered independent-generation power assumption, and a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed (no rationale recorded). We release the authoritative archived artifacts so other researchers can reproduce the accounting and execute the recommended follow-ups (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden tasks, multi-model evaluations, expanded verifier coverage) to more robustly evaluate GVR’s operational value for NetOps.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
